description: Two binary clock dividers whose matching stages are exclusive-ORed together, the four results coming out as gates and as one mixed voltage

params.text: Sets how much that division adds into the OUT and SLEW jacks, 0V to 5V; it changes nothing at the division's own gate output
Sets the rate limit on the SLEW output, from about 18000 volts per second fully anticlockwise down to 1 volt per second fully clockwise

inputs.text: Steps the first divider on each rise above 1V
Steps the second divider on each rise above 1V

outputs.text: 5V while the two dividers disagree at their first stage, which with one input patched is a plain division of that clock by two
5V while the two dividers disagree at their second stage, which with one input patched is a plain division of that clock by four
5V while the two dividers disagree at their third stage, which with one input patched is a plain division of that clock by eight
5V while the two dividers disagree at their fourth stage, which with one input patched is a plain division of that clock by sixteen
The gain knobs of whichever divisions are high at that moment, added together, so it steps between 0V and 20V and never goes negative
The OUT voltage passed through a rate limiter set by the SLEW knob

notes: with one input patched the gate outputs are a binary divider of that clock; with both patched each is the exclusive-OR of the two dividers, a one-bit ring modulator.
every output is unipolar, so a patch treating OUT as audio needs a DC blocker or a high-pass filter after it.
the four gain knobs come up fully anticlockwise, so OUT and SLEW stay at 0V until one of them is raised, even with a clock running.

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
